info.name: OneTicket Milestone 2 APIs
info.description: Requests generated from the Milestone 2 OpenAPI contracts. The contracts are currently drafts (0.1.0-draft). Requests intentionally use no authentication for the current Milestone 3 setup; folder descriptions record the intended future role policy. Update the local environment ports when Inventory & Orders and Ticketing are assigned ports.

Return only events starting at or after this instant (inclusive), with explicit offset ([API-05]); compared as an instant, independently of the venues' offsets.
Return only events starting before this instant (exclusive), with explicit offset ([API-05]); compared as an instant, independently of the venues' offsets. Must not precede `fromDate`.
Return only events held at this venue.

request.description:
Returns one page of events matching the filters. All filters are optional and combine with AND;
no implicit date filter is applied, so clients browsing upcoming events pass `fromDate`.

Filters: `title`, `fromDate`, `toDate`, `venueId`, `city`, `country`, `genre`. Sort fields:
`startsAt`, `title` (whitelist, [API-35]); ties are broken by ascending event `id`.

Each event's `startsAt` is in the local time of its venue ([API-55]): the offset is the one in
force at the venue on that date (e.g. `+02:00` for Turin in summer, `+01:00` in winter), not the
caller's. Items of one page can therefore carry different offsets. `fromDate`, `toDate` and the
`startsAt` sort compare instants, whatever offset is sent or returned.

Clients display `startsAt` as returned, in the venue's local time, and convert `salesOpenAt` to
their own time zone ([API-56]).

Public: callable without a token ([ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-public-seat-map.md)).

request.description:
Returns one page of the event's seats with their current state and price. Seats are ordered by
ascending seat `id`; no other sort order and no filters are offered.

The seat map is not cacheable ([API-31]): the response is `no-store`. Each item carries the
seat's `etag`, to be sent as `If-Match` when placing a hold on that seat.

Public: callable without a token ([ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-public-seat-map.md)).

Returns the seat with its current state and price. The `ETag` is the seat's row version, to be
sent as `If-Match` when placing a hold ([API-29]). The representation must be revalidated on
every use (`no-cache`, [API-31]); `If-None-Match` answers `304` when the seat is unchanged.

Public: callable without a token ([ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-public-seat-map.md)).


Get one seat of an event

Authentication is intentionally disabled in this collection for the current milestone.

header.description: Client-generated UUID identifying one logical operation, reused on every retry of it ([API-24]); retained for 24 hours.
ETag of the seat named in the body, as returned by the seat map or `getEventSeat`.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Customer operation. Moves one FREE seat of the event to HELD for the calling customer and
creates a hold that expires at `expiresAt` (time to live set in configuration, about ten
minutes, [OPS-26]). Several seats are held with one hold each.

- Of several concurrent requests for the same seat, at most one succeeds ([BIZ-04]); the others
  fail fast with `409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` and should refresh the seat map ([API-20], [API-21]).
- `If-Match` (optional) carries the seat's `ETag` as read from the seat map: if the seat changed
  since, the request fails with `412 SEAT_VERSION_MISMATCH` ([API-29]).
- A customer holds at most a configured number of active seats ([BIZ-08]); beyond it the request
  fails with `409 HOLD_LIMIT_REACHED`.
- Holds are only granted while the event's sales are open (`409 SALES_CLOSED`).


Hold a seat

header.description: ETag of the hold as last read; the update fails with 412 if the hold changed since.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Customer operation. Moves the expiry of an ACTIVE hold later, with a JSON Merge Patch
(RFC 7396, [API-15]); `expiresAt` is the only patchable field. Setting the same `expiresAt`
again returns the same result.

The new `expiresAt` must be later than the current one; a request outside the extension policy
answers `422 HOLD_EXTENSION_NOT_ALLOWED`.

**TODO** [BIZ-27]: the hold extension policy (maximum hold lifetime, number and length of
extensions) is still to be defined.

`If-Match` (optional) carries the hold's `ETag`: a stale one answers `412`.


Extend a hold's expiry

Authentication is intentionally disabled in this collection for the current milestone.

header.description: Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Customer operation. Releases the hold and frees its seat (HELD -> FREE, [BIZ-03]). Idempotent:
releasing a hold that is already RELEASED or EXPIRED answers `204` again ([API-14]).

Releasing a hold that belongs to a PENDING order cancels that order and releases its other
holds ([BIZ-13], cancellation reason `HOLD_RELEASED`). A CONFIRMED hold (seat SOLD) cannot be
released: `409 HOLD_CONFIRMED`; refunds go through Payments ([BIZ-07], [BIZ-14]).


Release a hold

Authentication is intentionally disabled in this collection for the current milestone.

header.description: Client-generated UUID identifying one logical operation, reused on every retry of it ([API-24]); retained for 24 hours.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Customer operation. Creates a PENDING order ([BIZ-11]) for one or more of the caller's ACTIVE
holds of the same event, then requests the payment from Payments; the order carries the
resulting `paymentId`, which the client uses to pay at the PSP. The outcome of the payment is
observed on the order resource (`Location`): `PAID` on success ([BIZ-12]), `CANCELLED` on every
unsuccessful outcome ([BIZ-13]).

`Idempotency-Key` guarantees that a retried purchase never creates a second order nor a second
payment ([BIZ-17]). Each order line stores the seat price at creation time.

**Call to Payments.** The payment is requested with Payments' `createPayment`
(`POST /api/v1/payments`, [payments_api.yaml](payments_api.yaml)):

- authenticated with the service's own Keycloak client-credentials token, `service` role
  ([ARCH-31]); the customer's token is never forwarded;
- body: `orderId`, `customerId` (the `sub` claim of the caller's token, so Payments can restrict
  payment and refund reads to that customer) and `amount` (the order `total`);
- `Idempotency-Key`: a UUID generated once per order and stored with it, reused on every retry
  of the call ([API-24]), so a retry never registers a second payment; Payments also refuses a
  second payment for the same order (`409 ORDER_ALREADY_HAS_PAYMENT`);
- never inside the database transaction ([SVC-19]); if Payments or the PSP is unavailable the
  request fails with `503 PAYMENTS_UNAVAILABLE`, and the client retries with the same
  `Idempotency-Key`.


Create an order from held seats

request.description:
Customer operation. Cancels a PENDING order (PENDING -> CANCELLED, reason `CUSTOMER_REQUEST`,
[BIZ-13]) and releases its holds, freeing their seats. The cancellation is inspectable on the
order (`status`, `cancelledAt`, `cancellationReason`). Cancelling an already CANCELLED order
returns it unchanged. A PAID or REFUNDED order cannot be cancelled (`409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE`,
[BIZ-15]); refunds go through Payments ([BIZ-14]).

**Open point** [BIZ-28]: the outcome of a cancellation while the order's payment is still in
progress at the PSP is not defined yet.

header.description: ETag of the JSON representation held by the client; the server answers 304 if it still matches.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Customer operation. Returns one of the caller's tickets; another customer's ticket answers
`404` ([API-18]). The representation is chosen with `Accept` ([API-41], [API-43]):

- `application/json`: the ticket metadata, with an `ETag`; `If-None-Match` answers `304` when
  the ticket is unchanged.
- `application/pdf`: the ticket document, streamed by Ticketing from object storage
  ([ARCH-19]), which is never exposed to clients. While the PDF is not rendered yet
  (`documentReady` is `false`, [BIZ-21]) the request fails with `409 TICKET_DOCUMENT_NOT_READY`.
  A REVOKED ticket's document is still served, as a record of the purchase.


Get a ticket or its PDF document

Authentication is intentionally disabled in this collection for the current milestone.

header.description: Client-generated UUID identifying one logical operation, reused on every retry of it ([API-24]); retained for 24 hours.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Gate-staff operation. Validates the ticket read from the QR code against the event the gate
serves, and admits it if valid. Built to answer fast: one lookup by ticket id and one
conditional update.

- First scan of a VALID ticket for this event: the ticket becomes SCANNED and the admission is
  recorded: `201`, admit ([BIZ-26]). Of several concurrent scans of the same ticket, exactly
  one is admitted.
- Later scans: `409 TICKET_ALREADY_SCANNED`, always with the same body, carrying the admitting
  scan (`firstScan`) so staff can see when and where the ticket entered ([BIZ-26]). State does
  not change.
- REVOKED ticket (order refunded): `409 TICKET_REVOKED`, refuse.
- Ticket for another event: `422 TICKET_WRONG_EVENT`, refuse.
- Unknown ticket id (e.g. a forged QR code): `404 TICKET_NOT_FOUND`, refuse.

`Idempotency-Key` is required so that a scanner retrying after a lost response gets the
original `201` replayed, not a misleading `409 TICKET_ALREADY_SCANNED` for a ticket it has just
admitted. A new physical scan uses a new key.

**TODO** [ARCH-03]: which events a gate-staff member may scan is still to be defined; this draft
accepts any `gate-staff` token.

item.name: Payments
item.description: Source: docs/milestones/milestone2/payments_api.yaml (OpenAPI 3.1.0, 0.1.0-draft). Current requests use no authentication. Future contract policy: Customer or service role depending on the operation; PSP webhooks use the provider signature when authentication is implemented.

header.description: Client-generated UUID identifying one logical operation, reused on every retry of it ([API-24]); retained for 24 hours.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Service operation, called by Inventory & Orders after creating a PENDING order ([ARCH-31]); not
routed by the edge. Registers the payment at the PSP and returns it PENDING; the customer then
pays at the PSP with the payment `id`.

- An order has at most one payment: a second payment for the same order with a different
  `Idempotency-Key` fails with `409 ORDER_ALREADY_HAS_PAYMENT`, so a retried purchase never
  charges twice ([BIZ-17]). Retries of the same attempt reuse the key and get the stored
  response.
- If the PSP cannot be reached, nothing is created and the call fails with
  `503 PSP_UNAVAILABLE`; the caller retries with the same key.
- A payment not completed at the PSP within the payment timeout (set in configuration,
  [OPS-26]) becomes TIMED_OUT.


Request the payment of an order

Authentication is intentionally disabled in this collection for the current milestone.

header.description: ETag of the representation held by the client; the server answers 304 if it still matches.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Customer or service operation. A customer reads only the payments of their own orders; another
customer's payment answers `404` ([API-18]). `If-None-Match` answers `304` when the payment is
unchanged.


Get a payment

Authentication is intentionally disabled in this collection for the current milestone.

header.description: Client-generated UUID identifying one logical operation, reused on every retry of it ([API-24]); retained for 24 hours.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
Customer operation. Requests the refund of the whole amount of one of the caller's SUCCEEDED
payments ([BIZ-14]); single tickets cannot be refunded. The refund is executed at the PSP
asynchronously: the response is `202` with the PENDING refund, whose progress is observed at
`Location` ([API-17]). On success the payment becomes REFUNDED and Inventory & Orders is
notified, which applies `PAID -> REFUNDED` to the order and frees its seats ([BIZ-07]).

- Another customer's payment answers `404` ([API-18]).
- A payment that is not SUCCEEDED cannot be refunded: `409 PAYMENT_NOT_REFUNDABLE`.
- A payment has at most one active or succeeded refund: a new request while one is PENDING or
  SUCCEEDED fails with `409 REFUND_ALREADY_REQUESTED`; after a FAILED refund a new one may be
  requested.

**TODO** [BIZ-29]: the refund eligibility policy (deadline relative to the event, retained
fees) is still to be defined.


Request the refund of a paid order

Authentication is intentionally disabled in this collection for the current milestone.

header.description: ETag of the representation held by the client; the server answers 304 if it still matches.
Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

header.description: Correlation id of the request; generated by the server when absent and returned on the response ([OPS-12]).

request.description:
PSP operation ([ADR-0003](../../adr/0003-psp-webhook-authentication.md)). Authenticated by the
PSP signature over the raw body, verified before parsing; no Keycloak token.

- Deliveries are at least once: an event whose `id` was already processed answers `204` without
  re-executing ([BIZ-18]).
- Events may arrive out of order ([BIZ-16]): an event that would cause an illegal transition
  (e.g. a failure after a success, a success after a timeout) is recorded and answers `204`
  without changing state; the late-success case is open (**TODO** [BIZ-10], [BIZ-28]).
- An event for an unknown payment or refund is recorded and answers `204`, so the PSP does not
  redeliver it forever.
- A processed outcome is published to Inventory & Orders as an asynchronous message
  ([BIZ-12], [ARCH-16]).

The payload shape follows the PSP sandbox; the schema lists the fields Payments relies on.

request.description:
Service operation ([ARCH-31]). Queues a new copy of a SENT or FAILED email, e.g. when the
customer did not receive it or sending gave up. The copy is a new email record with its own
`id`, `resendOf` pointing at the original, whose own record is left unchanged. Sending is
deferred: the response is `202` with the QUEUED copy, whose progress is observed at `Location`
([API-17]). The recipient address and the ticket attachments are resolved again at send time.
